articles.title: Home Assistant brings alert cards to any dashboard
articles.dek: A visual editor makes household warnings easier to place, with separate colours for alert and clear states.
body: Home Assistant adds a visual editor for its alert card, making it possible to place and configure the warning display on any dashboard without writing YAML. The card can highlight triggered alarms, active binary sensors, open covers and unlocked, open or jammed locks.

The editor separates the colour used during an alert from the colour shown when it is clear. Alerts default to red, and an optional pulse respects the viewer’s reduced-motion preference by keeping the colour steady.

The built-in home and security dashboards keep their existing behaviour. Anyone who added an alert card through YAML needs to replace the old color option with alert_color; setting it to none keeps alerts uncoloured.

pullRequests.title: Add visual editor for the alert card and add clear color
Add alert card documentation

media.alt: Four Home Assistant alert cards showing motion, security and door states with coloured or plain backgrounds.
media.caption: Alert cards can distinguish the alert colour from the colour shown when clear.

articles.title: ESPHome connects USB microphones and speakers
articles.dek: Compatible ESP32 boards can record and play through USB sound cards, microphones and speakerphones.
body: ESPHome adds USB audio for makers who want to connect an off-the-shelf microphone, sound card or speakerphone to an ESP32 with USB host hardware. Separate microphone and speaker components capture sound and play audio, including through ESPHome’s existing speaker media player.

Devices can be connected and removed while the system runs. Each stream uses a chosen audio format; unsupported formats are reported in the logs. Volume and mute commands reach the audio device when it provides those controls.
Related work adjusts how the ESP32-S2 and S3 share their USB buffers, making room for a microphone and speaker together. The connection requires an ESP32 variant with USB host support.

pullRequests.title: [usb_audio] Add USB Audio Class (UAC) host support
[usb_host] Size the FIFO split on ESP32-S2/S3 from periodic packet requests
[audio] Compute frames_to_microseconds() in 64 bits

articles.title: Home Assistant reads HAVEN air monitors without a cloud account
articles.dek: Compatible room and central monitors supply air-quality readings over the home network.
body: HAVEN Room Air Monitor and Central Air Monitor devices gain a local connection to Home Assistant. The integration reads air-quality or airflow sensors according to the product, using the home network without requiring a cloud account.

Automatic discovery finds compatible monitors, while manual setup accepts their hostname or IP address. The room monitor requires firmware 19 or later; the central monitor requires version 2.4.2 or later. Readings refresh once a minute.
This first step covers sensors, not HAVEN Controller devices or relay controls. It is krhtzoa’s first contribution to Home Assistant Core.

pullRequests.title: Add HAVEN IAQ integration
Add HAVEN IAQ integration documentation

articles.title: Music Assistant controls music started in other Raumfeld apps
articles.dek: Spotify Connect and playback from the Raumfeld app gain track information and controls inside Music Assistant.
body: Music Assistant shows and controls music started outside its own interface on Teufel Raumfeld systems. Spotify Connect and music or radio started in the Raumfeld app report their source and playing item, rather than only the address carrying the audio.

Pause, previous, next and seeking are available where the Raumfeld host supports them for that source. A stopped source can also resume until Music Assistant's idle timeout. Simanias tested Spotify Connect, Tidal through the Raumfeld app and TuneIn radio.

pullRequests.title: Control playback started outside Music Assistant on Raumfeld players

articles.title: Home Assistant lets AI assistants answer questions about past readings
articles.dek: A history tool supplies recorded statistics rather than only the current value.
body: AI assistants connected through Home Assistant’s language-model interface gain a way to answer questions about earlier readings. A history tool supplies long-term statistics for each requested entity, giving the assistant information beyond its present value.

The response includes units and local timestamps, with the size of each time interval chosen to suit the requested span. This covers recorded statistics; a timeline of individual state changes remains outside the new tool.

pullRequests.title: Add get_history tool to the Home Assistant LLM API

articles.title: ESPHome controls Home Assistant lights with familiar light actions
articles.dek: Physical buttons, displays and automations can follow a light’s brightness and colour as well as change them.
body: ESPHome adds a light that mirrors a chosen Home Assistant light and controls it through the native connection. Makers can use ordinary ESPHome light actions to build a dimming button or display control while following changes made elsewhere.

Egor Vorontsov’s implementation follows the light’s state, brightness, colour and supported colour modes. After sending a change, it waits for Home Assistant to confirm the result; if the request cannot be sent or no report arrives, it returns to the last reported state instead of continuing to show an unconfirmed setting.

pullRequests.title: [homeassistant] Add the light platform

articles.title: Music Assistant corrects duplicate and mistaken artist credits
articles.dek: Verified identities bring duplicate artists together, while retagged files and short Plex names keep the right credits.
body: Music Assistant brings duplicate library artists together when their tags, streaming links or recordings establish the same MusicBrainz identity. For example, Sydney Symphony and Sydney Symphony Orchestra can become one entry. A match based only on a name search is deliberately insufficient, protecting different artists who share a name.

Related library corrections stop an old artist remaining beside a replacement after a local music file is moved and retagged. Existing affected libraries need another retag or rescan to refresh. Albums assembled only from tags without their own folder can retain the old link.

Plex tracks also require an exact artist-name match after searching the library. That prevents a short name such as LEN from incorrectly choosing Amelie Lens. OzGav supplies the identity and retagging changes, with Chris Roberts correcting Plex's lookup.

Fix Plex track artist library lookup

articles.title: ESPHome dims LED strips to an estimated current budget
articles.dek: An optional limit follows changing colours and effects across addressable-light drivers.
body: ESPHome adds an optional current budget for addressable LED strips. It estimates demand from the colours and brightness of each displayed frame, then reduces the physical output uniformly when the estimate exceeds the configured limit.

Marcus Voß’s work applies across addressable-light drivers, including effects and transitions, without changing the brightness setting shown to the user. The estimate depends on the maker’s per-channel current values; it is not a current measurement, and rounding can leave a small overshoot. His companion guide is his first contribution to ESPHome’s documentation.

articles.title: HACS raises its Home Assistant minimum to 2026.10.2
articles.dek: The compatibility requirement moves from March 2025 to this month's patch release.
body: HACS raises its declared Home Assistant minimum from 2025.3.0 to 2026.10.2. Households on older versions need to update Home Assistant before adopting a HACS version carrying the change.

articles.title: Home Assistant clears unused dashboards and blueprints in batches
articles.dek: Selection mode also removes labels and uninstalls Marketplace items, with safeguards for items still in use.
body: Home Assistant extends selection mode to dashboards, blueprints, labels and the Marketplace’s installed list. Owners can select several unwanted items and clear them together instead of repeating the same operation one at a time.

Blueprints still used by automations or scripts are skipped, as are built-in dashboards and dashboards configured in YAML. Deleting a label removes it from the areas, devices and entities that used it. Marketplace uninstalls delete an item’s configured connections, devices and entities before uninstalling its files, following the existing single-item process.

articles.title: Music Assistant gives car buttons shorter skips for spoken audio
articles.dek: Android Auto's steering-wheel controls move through an audiobook or podcast without changing the episode.
body: Music Assistant maps Android Auto's steering-wheel Next and Previous buttons to a thirty-second skip forward and a ten-second skip back for audiobooks and podcast episodes. On-screen Next and Previous still change the playing item.

Andrii Mitnovych also prevents a Next press on the final queue item from leaving the phone's position stuck at zero when the server ignores the request. That preserves the real starting point for a following thirty-second skip.

pullRequests.title: Keep episode progress when the server ignores Next

articles.title: Home Assistant gives thermostat controls clearer spoken labels
articles.dek: Screen readers gain temperature units and names for range selectors and adjustment buttons.
body: Home Assistant improves the information its thermostat controls give to screen readers. Temperature labels include their units, and the circular slider receives the missing labels for the current value and its upper and lower limits.

The buttons that choose which end of a temperature range to adjust, along with the plus and minus buttons, also gain labels. These labels distinguish the two ends of a temperature range when adjusting a thermostat without relying on its visual layout.
